ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a coordinate-axis schematic diagram, with x and 8 marked on the horizontal axis, and y and 5 marked on the vertical axis. The gray rectangle S1 is located in the upper left, with its left side against the vertical axis, its right side at the vertical line x, its top side at height 5, and its bottom side at height y, so the width of S1 is x and its height is 5-y. The gray rectangle S2 is located in the lower right, with its left side starting from x, its right side reaching 8, its bottom side against the horizontal axis, and its top side at height y, so the width of S2 is 8-x and its height is y. Reasoning: The problem says S1 and S2 have equal areas, therefore x(5-y)=(8-x)y. Expanding gives 5x-xy=8y-xy. Cancelling -xy on both sides gives 5x=8y. Therefore x/y=8/5, so x:y=8:5.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a coordinate rectangle split by the vertical line at x and the horizontal line at y. From the image, S1 is the upper-left rectangle with width x and height 5-y, while S2 is the lower-right rectangle with width 8-x and height y. From the text, their areas are equal. Set x(5-y)=(8-x)y, expand to 5x-xy=8y-xy, cancel -xy, and obtain 5x=8y. Therefore x:y=8:5.
